segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Forty-Six. Construct a square on a given segment. Let A B be the given segment. We construct a square on segment A B.

subsegments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Forty-Six. Construct a square on a given segment. Let A B be the given segment. We construct a square on segment A B.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: From point A on segment A B, construct segment A C at right angles to A B, and cut off segment A D equal to segment A B. Through point D construct segment D E parallel to A B, and through point B construct segment B E parallel to A D, completing parallelogram A D E B.

subsegments.text: From point A on segment A B, construct segment A C at right angles to A B, and cut off segment A D equal to segment A B. Through point D construct segment D E parallel to A B, and through point B construct segment B E parallel to A D, completing parallelogram A D E B.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: In parallelogram A D E B, opposite sides are equal: A B equals D E, and A D equals B E. Since A B was made equal to A D, all four sides B A, A D, D E, and E B are equal to one another, so parallelogram A D E B is equilateral. Furthermore, since transversal A D cuts parallels A B and D E, interior angles B A D and A D E sum to two right angles. Because angle B A D is a right angle, angle A D E is also a right angle; and since opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, angles A B E and B E D are also right angles, making A D E B right-angled. Since figure A D E B is both equilateral and right-angled, it is a square constructed on segment A B, as was required to do.
